summary: Implementation notes for the compiler and interpreter of the Data Reconfiguration Service. It lists new features of the language, such as pattern descriptors for finding EBCDIC characters, assignment of all attributes of one identifier to another, and concatenation.

eli5.summary: Extra notes for the translator machine builders, about new things it can do when it reads and moves data around.

questions: what are the data reconfiguration service language features
how does the drs compiler work
subtitle: New compiler features and interpreter architecture for the Data Reconfiguration Service.

tldr.problem: Data across a network is stored in different representations and organizations. A system must convert between these formats while letting users access data without knowing implementation details.
tldr.mechanism: The DRS compiler interprets a language for describing and transforming data. New features include pattern descriptors for finding character sequences, attribute copying, concatenation, type conversions, and an interpreter machine with instructions for complex data operations.
tldr.outcome: Network data can be reformatted and accessed uniformly despite differences in how individual hosts store it.

facts.label: Numeric types supported
facts.value: Binary, octal, hex, decimal, signed binary

today: RFC 194 documents implementation details of the Data Reconfiguration Service from July 1971. It was part of early work on network data management to handle heterogeneous host computers across the ARPANET.

sections.title: New Language Features
sections.content: RFC 194 documents enhancements to the Data Reconfiguration Service language compiler and interpreter. The DRS language describes how to find, read, and transform data across heterogeneous network hosts. New features include: pattern descriptors using S(#,E,,l) to find up to 256 EBCDIC characters; the assignment operator .<=. to copy all attributes (length, type, contents) from one identifier to another; concatenation S .<=. T || X to combine data; new type constructors ED and AD for EBCDIC and ASCII decimal encoding; and a type function T(X) returning the data type of an identifier, complementing existing length L(X) and value V(X) functions.
sections.eli5: The translator learns: 'find a run of these characters', 'copy this with all its properties', 'stick two things together', and 'tell me what kind of thing this is'.

sections.title: New Syntax and Grammar
sections.content: The revised syntax formalizes how forms (rules for data processing) are structured. A form contains one or more rules, each with an input stream and output stream. Identifiers are alphanumeric labels. Descriptors specify replication (how many items), datatype (binary, octal, hex, EBCDIC, ASCII, ASCII decimal, EBCDIC decimal, signed binary, or user-defined), value expression, and length. Comparators test numeric or string relationships. The grammar supports arithmetic expressions with operators (+, -, *, /), literal values with type indicators, and control options. An important addition is the SFUR control mechanism which modifies behavior (S, F, U, SR, FR, UR options with arithmetic expressions).
sections.eli5: The grammar now says clearly how to write: which input to read, what data type it is, how many to read, what to do with it, and where to write the result.

sections.title: The Form Interpreter Machine
sections.content: The RFC describes an interpreter virtual machine that executes compiled DRS instructions. The machine contains a CPU with an arithmetic logic unit and instruction decoder, state registers tracking execution, an instruction sequence storage, a label table, a literal and identifier pool, and a variable-length string area. The CPU maintains an instruction counter and instruction register, decodes operation codes, and dispatches to instruction interpreter routines. A run-time operand stack holds values during computation. This architecture provides a powerful instruction set for operations too complex for efficient compilation, letting compiler writers focus on higher-level optimization while the interpreter handles complex data transformation operations.
sections.eli5: The interpreter is a simple machine: it reads instructions one by one, looks up values in tables, does arithmetic, and outputs results. A smart compiler can hand hard problems to this machine instead of trying to compile them directly.
